verses.text: One man dey for di land of Uz, im name na Job. Dat man dey blameless and honest, e dey fear God and e dey turn away from evil.
Seven sons and three daughters dey born for am.
Im property na 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 500 pairs of oxen and 500 female donkeys, and very plenty servants, so dat dis man na di greatest of all di people of di east.
Im sons dey go dey hold feast for di house of each one for im birthday, and dem dey send call dem three sisters to come eat and drink with dem.

When di days of dem feast don finish, Job go send for dem and make dem holy. E go wake early for morning and offer burnt sacrifices according to di number of dem all. Because Job talk say, “Maybe my sons don sin and curse God for dem heart.” Na so Job dey do always.
Now one day di sons of God come to stand before di Lord, and Satan come among dem too.
Di Lord talk to Satan say, “Wia you dey come from?” Den Satan answer di Lord say, “From dey waka go and come for di earth and from dey waka up and down inside am.”
Di Lord talk to Satan say, “You don look my servant Job? Because nobody like am dey for di earth, one blameless and honest man, wey dey fear God and dey turn away from evil.”
Den Satan answer di Lord say, “Job dey fear God for nothing?
You no don put fence round am, round im house and round all wey e get, for every side? You don bless di work of im hands, and im property don increase for di land.
But stretch your hand now and touch all wey e get, and e go curse you for your face.”
Di Lord talk to Satan say, “Look, all wey e get dey your power. Only on am, no put your hand.” So Satan go out from di Lord presence.
One day when im sons and im daughters dey eat and drink wine for dem eldest brother house,
messenger come to Job and talk say, “Di oxen dey plough and di donkeys dey feed beside dem,
and di Sabeans attack and carry dem go. Yes, dem don kill di servants with sword, and na only me escape to come tell you.”
As e still dey talk, another one come and talk say, “God fire don fall from heaven and burn di sheep and di servants and finish dem, and na only me escape to come tell you.”

As e still dey talk, another one come and talk say, “Di Chaldeans form three groups, attack di camels and carry dem go. Yes, dem don kill di servants with sword, and na only me escape to come tell you.”
As e still dey talk, another one come and talk say, “Your sons and your daughters dey eat and drink wine for dem eldest brother house,
and look, big wind come from di wilderness and hit di four corners of di house, and e fall on di young people, and dem don die, and na only me escape to come tell you.”
Den Job stand up, tear im robe, shave im head, fall down for ground and worship.
E talk say, “Naked I come out from my mama belly, and naked I go return there. Di Lord give, and di Lord don take. Make dem bless di name of di Lord.”
For all dis Job no sin and e no blame God for wrong.
Again one day di sons of God come to stand before di Lord, and Satan come among dem too to stand before di Lord.
Di Lord talk to Satan say, “Wia you dey come from?” Satan answer di Lord say, “From dey waka go and come for di earth and from dey waka up and down inside am.”

Di Lord talk to Satan say, “You don look my servant Job? Because nobody like am dey for di earth, one blameless and honest man, wey dey fear God and dey turn away from evil. E still dey hold im honesty, even though you push me against am to ruin am for no reason.”
Satan answer di Lord say, “Skin for skin! Yes, all wey man get, e go give am for im life.
But stretch your hand now and touch im bone and im flesh, and e go curse you for your face.”
Di Lord talk to Satan say, “Look, e dey your hand. Only spare im life.”
So Satan go out from di Lord presence and strike Job with painful sores from di sole of im foot reach di top of im head.
E take broken pot piece to scratch imself, and e sit among di ashes.
Den im wife talk to am say, “You still dey hold your honesty? Curse God and die.”
But e talk to am say, “You dey talk like one of di foolish women dey talk. Wetin? We go receive good from God hand, and we no go receive evil?” For all dis Job no sin with im lips.

Now when Job three friends hear about all dis evil wey don come on am, dem come, each one from im own place: Eliphaz di Temanite, Bildad di Shuhite and Zophar di Naamathite. Dem agree together to come mourn with am and to comfort am.
When dem lift dem eyes from far and no know am, dem raise dem voice and cry. Each one tear im robe and throw dust toward heaven on dem heads.
So dem sit down with am for ground seven days and seven nights, and nobody talk one word to am, because dem see say im sorrow big well well.
After dis Job open im mouth and curse im day.
Job answer say,
“Make di day wey dem born me perish, di night wey talk say, ‘Dem don conceive boy.’
Make dat day turn darkness. No make God from above look for am, and no make light shine on am.
Make darkness and di shadow of death take am as dem own. Make cloud stay on am. Make all wey dey make day black frighten am.
As for dat night, make darkness seize am. No make e rejoice among di days of di year. No make e enter di number of di months.
Look, make dat night dey empty. No make any joyful cry enter am.
Make dem curse am wey dey curse di day, wey ready to wake up leviathan.
Make di stars of im evening dey dark. Make e look for light, but e no go get, and no make e see di eyelids of di morning,
because e no close di doors of my mama belly and no hide trouble from my eyes.
Why I no die from di belly? Why I no give up my spirit when my mama born me?
Why di knees receive me? Or why di breasts, so dat I go suck?
Because now I for don lie down and dey quiet. I for don sleep, den I for don rest,
with kings and advisers of di earth, wey build empty ruined places for dem self,
or with princes wey get gold, wey fill dem houses with silver,
or like hidden baby wey die before time, I for no dey, like babies wey never see light.
Dere di wicked stop to cause trouble. Dere di tired dey rest.
Dere di prisoners dey rest together. Dem no dey hear di voice of di slave driver.
Di small and di great dey dere. Di servant free from im master.
Why dem give light to am wey dey misery, life to di bitter for soul,
wey long for death, but e no come, and dig for am more than for hidden treasure,
wey rejoice well well and dey glad when dem find di grave?
Why dem give light to man wey im way dey hidden, wey God don fence round?
Because my sighing dey come before I eat, and my groaning dey pour out like water.
Because di thing wey I fear don come on me, and wetin I dey fear don reach me.
I no dey at ease, I no dey quiet, I no get rest, but trouble dey come.”
Den Eliphaz di Temanite answer say,
“If person try to talk with you, e go pain you? But who fit hold imself from talking?
Look, you don teach plenty people, and you don strengthen weak hands.
Your words don support am wey dey fall, and you don make weak knees strong.
But now e don reach you, and you faint. E touch you, and you dey troubled.
No be your fear of God na your confidence? No be di honesty of your ways na your hope?
Remember, I beg you, who don perish before, being innocent? Or where dem don cut off di honest?
According to wetin I don see, dem wey plough wickedness and plant trouble go harvest di same.
By God breath dem perish, and by di blast of im anger dem finish.
Di roar of di lion, di voice of di fierce lion and di teeth of di young lions dey broken.
Di old lion dey perish because e no get prey, and di lioness pikin dem dey scatter.
Now one thing come to me quietly. My ear catch small whisper of am.
For thoughts from di visions of di night, when deep sleep fall on people,
fear come on me, and shaking, wey make all my bones tremble.
Den one spirit pass before my face, and di hair of my body stand up.
E stand still, but I no fit see how e look. One form dey before my eyes. Silence dey, den I hear voice say,
‘Mortal man go dey more righteous than God? Man go dey more pure than im Maker?
Look, e no put trust for im servants. E dey blame im angels for mistake.
How much more dem wey dey stay for houses of clay, wey dem foundation dey for dust, wey dem dey crush before moth!
Between morning and evening dem dey destroy dem. Dem dey perish forever and nobody notice.
No be say dem tent rope don pull out inside dem? Dem die, and dem die without wisdom.’”
“Call now. Anybody dey wey go answer you? To which of di holy ones you go turn?
Because anger dey kill di foolish man, and jealousy dey kill di simple.
I don see di foolish dey take root, but suddenly I curse im home.
Im pikin dem dey far from safety. Dem dey crush for di gate, and nobody dey to save dem,
wey hungry people dey eat dem harvest, and take am even from di thorns. Trap dey open mouth for dem property.
Because suffering no dey come from dust, and trouble no dey spring from di ground,
but man dey born for trouble, like sparks wey dey fly up.
But as for me, I for look for God. I for put my case before God,
wey dey do great things wey nobody fit understand, wonderful things wey no get number,
wey dey give rain to di earth and dey send water to di fields,
so dat e dey lift up di low ones high, and dem wey dey mourn dey rise to safety.
E dey spoil di plans of di clever, so dat dem hands no fit finish dem work.
E dey catch di wise inside dem own cleverness, and di advice of di cunning dey rush down.
Dem dey meet darkness for daytime and dey grope for midday like night.
But e dey save from di sword of dem mouth, even di poor from di hand of di mighty.
So di poor get hope, and injustice close im mouth.
Look, happy na di man wey God dey correct. So no look down di discipline of di Almighty.
Because e dey wound and e dey bandage. E dey hurt and im hands dey heal.
E go save you for six troubles. Yes, for seven, no evil go touch you.
For hunger e go save you from death, for war from di power of di sword.
E go hide you from di whip of di tongue, and you no go fear destruction when e come.
For destruction and hunger you go laugh, and you no go fear di wild animals of di earth.
Because you go dey agreement with di stones of di field, and di wild animals of di field go dey peace with you.
You go know say your tent dey peace. You go check your sheep pen and you no go miss anything.
You go know too say your family go big, and your pikin dem go be like di grass of di earth.
You go reach your grave for full old age, like bundle of grain wey dem carry come for im season.
Look, we don search dis out, and e dey so. Hear am and know am for your own good.”
Den Job answer say,
“Oh, if dem fit weigh my pain, and put all my trouble for scale!
Because now e go heavy pass di sand of di seas, so my words don dey rash.
Because di arrows of di Almighty dey inside me, and my spirit dey drink dem poison. God terrors line up against me.
Wild donkey dey cry when e get grass? Or ox dey cry over im food?
Person fit eat food wey no get taste without salt? Or taste dey for di white of egg?
My soul refuse to touch dem. Dem be like food wey dey disgust me.
Oh, if I fit get wetin I dey ask for, if God fit give me wetin I dey long for,
even say e go please God to crush me, say e go let go im hand and cut me off!
Make dis still be my comfort, yes, make I rejoice for pain wey no dey spare, say I no deny di words of di Holy One.
Wetin be my strength, say I go hope? Wetin be my end, say I go patient?
My strength na strength of stones? Or my flesh na bronze?
No be say no help dey inside me, and say wisdom don drive comot from me?
Person wey don almost faint suppose get kindness from im friend, even di one wey leave di fear of di Almighty.
My brothers don deceive me like stream, like di channel of streams wey dey pass,
wey dey black because of ice, and where snow dey hide,
di time wey dem get warm, dem disappear. When e hot, dem dry from dem place.
Di caravans wey dey travel by dem way turn aside. Dem go up inside empty land and perish.
Di caravans of Tema look. Di groups of Sheba wait for dem.
Dem dey disappointed because dem don trust. Dem come reach there and dem confuse.
Because now una no be anything. Una see terror and una fear.
I talk say, ‘Give me something’? Or, ‘Give gift for me from una property’?
Or, ‘Save me from enemy hand’? Or, ‘Buy me back from di hand of di wicked’?
Teach me, and I go keep quiet. Make me understand where I don make mistake.
How strong honest words dey! But your correction, wetin e dey correct?
You think say you go correct words, since di speeches of person wey dey desperate na like wind?
Yes, you for even cast lots for di orphan and sell your friend.
So now, I beg you, look me, because I no go lie to your face.
Return now. No make injustice dey. Yes, return again. My case dey righteous.
Injustice dey for my tongue? My mouth no fit know wicked things?”
“No be say man dey work hard for earth? And im days no be like di days of hired worker?
Like servant wey dey long for shade, like hired worker wey dey wait for im pay,
so dem don give me months of misery, and night wey dey tire me dem don appoint am for me.
When I lie down, I dey talk say, ‘When I go stand up, and night go finish?’ I dey turn up and down until day break.
Worms and lumps of dust cover my flesh. My skin dey close and dey break open again.
My days dey run pass weaver shuttle, and dem dey finish without hope.
Oh, remember say my life na breath. My eye no go see good again.
Di eye of di one wey dey see me no go see me again. Your eyes go dey on me, but I no go dey.
As cloud dey finish and disappear, so di one wey go down to Sheol no go come up again.
E no go return to im house again, and im place no go know am again.
So I no go hold my mouth. I go talk for di pain of my spirit. I go complain for di bitterness of my soul.
I be sea, or sea monster, say you put guard over me?
When I talk say, ‘My bed go comfort me, my couch go ease my complaint,’
den you dey frighten me with dreams and dey terrify me through visions,
so dat my soul choose to choke, death more than my bones.
I hate my life. I no wan live forever. Leave me alone, because my days na just breath.
Wetin be man, say you go make am big, say you go put your mind on am,
say you go visit am every morning and test am every moment?
How long you no go look away from me, and no go leave me alone until I swallow my spit?
If I don sin, wetin I do you, you wey dey watch people? Why you don set me as target for you, so dat I become load to myself?
Why you no forgive my disobedience and take away my wrong? Because now I go lie down for dust. You go look for me well well, but I no go dey.”
Den Bildad di Shuhite answer say,
“How long you go dey talk dis things? Di words of your mouth go be strong wind?
God dey twist justice? Or di Almighty dey twist righteousness?
If your pikin dem don sin against am, e don give dem into di hand of dem wrong.
If you go look for God well well and beg di Almighty,
if you pure and honest, sure now e go wake up for you and make di home of your righteousness prosper.
Even though your beginning small, your end go increase well well.
Because ask, I beg you, di former age, and prepare to learn wetin dem papa dem don search out,
because we be only yesterday people and we no know anything, because our days for earth na shadow,
dem no go teach you, tell you and talk words from dem heart?
Papyrus fit grow without swamp? Reeds fit grow without water?
While e still dey green and dem no cut am, e dey dry before any other plant.
So na di ways of all wey forget God. Di hope of di godless man go perish,
wey im confidence weak, wey im trust na spider web.
E go lean on im house, but e no go stand. E go hold am, but e no go last.
E dey green before di sun, and im branches dey spread over im garden.
Im roots wrap round di pile of stones. E see di place of stones.
If dem destroy am from im place, den e go deny am, dey talk say, ‘I no see you.’
Look, dis na di joy of im way. Out of di earth, others go spring up.
Look, God no go reject blameless man, and e no go support di wicked.
E go still fill your mouth with laughter and your lips with shouting.
Dem wey hate you go wear shame. Di tent of di wicked no go dey again.”
Den Job answer say,
“True true, I know say e dey so. But how man go fit dey righteous before God?
If e please am to argue with am, man no go fit answer am one for thousand.
E wise for heart and mighty for strength. Who don harden imself against am and prosper?
E dey move mountains, and dem no know am, when e overturn dem for im anger.
E dey shake di earth from im place, and im pillars dey tremble.
E dey command di sun, and e no dey rise, and e dey seal up di stars.
Na only e dey stretch out di heavens and dey waka on di waves of di sea.
E make di Bear, Orion, di Pleiades and di rooms of di south.
E dey do great things wey nobody fit find out, yes, wonderful things wey no get number.
Look, e dey pass me, and I no see am. E dey go too, but I no perceive am.
Look, e dey snatch away. Who fit stop am? Who go talk to am say, ‘Wetin you dey do?’
God no go withdraw im anger. Di helpers of Rahab bow down under am.
How much less I go answer am and choose my words to argue with am!
Even if I dey righteous, I no go answer am. I go beg my judge.
If I call and e answer me, I no go believe say e listen to my voice.
Because e dey break me with storm and dey increase my wounds for no reason.
E no go allow me catch my breath, but e dey fill me with bitterness.
If na matter of strength, look, e mighty! If na justice, who go summon am?
Even though I dey righteous, my own mouth go condemn me. Even though I blameless, e go show say I dey crooked.
I blameless. I no care for myself. I hate my life.
E all dey same. So I talk say e dey destroy di blameless and di wicked.
If di whip kill suddenly, e go laugh at di trial of di innocent.
Dem don give di earth into di hand of di wicked. E dey cover di faces of im judges. If no be am, who den?
Now my days dey run pass runner. Dem dey run away, dem no see good.
Dem don pass like fast boats, like eagle wey dey swoop on im prey.
If I talk say, ‘I go forget my complaint, I go remove my sad face and cheer up,’
I dey fear all my sorrows. I know say you no go hold me innocent.
Dem go condemn me. So why I go work hard for nothing?
If I wash myself with snow and make my hands clean well well,
still you go push me inside ditch, and my own clothes go hate me.
Because e no be man like me, say I go answer am, say we go come together for judgment.
No umpire dey between us, wey fit put im hand on us both.
Make am take im rod away from me, and make im terror no frighten me.
Den I go talk and I no go fear am, because I no dey so for myself.”
“My soul don tire for my life. I go give free way to my complaint. I go talk for di bitterness of my soul.
I go tell God say, ‘No condemn me. Show me why you dey argue with me.
E good for you say you go oppress, say you go look down di work of your hands and shine on di plan of di wicked?
You get eyes of flesh? Or you dey see as man dey see?
Your days na like di days of man, or your years like man days,
say you dey ask about my wrong and dey search for my sin,
even though you know say I no dey wicked, and nobody dey wey fit save from your hand?
Your hands don form me and shape me all round, yet you dey destroy me.
Remember, I beg you, say you make me like clay. You go bring me back to dust?
You no pour me out like milk and make me thick like cheese?
You cover me with skin and flesh and join me together with bones and veins.
You give me life and faithful love. Your care don keep my spirit.
Yet you hide dis things for your heart. I know say dis dey with you:
if I sin, den you dey watch me, and you no go free me from my wrong.
If I dey wicked, trouble dey for me! If I dey righteous, I no go lift my head, as I full with shame and I know my suffering.
If my head dey high, you dey hunt me like lion. Again you dey show yourself strong against me.
You dey renew your witnesses against me and dey increase your anger on me. Changes and war dey with me.
So why you bring me out of di belly? I for don give up my spirit, and no eye for don see me.
I for dey like say I no dey before. Dem for don carry me from di belly go di grave.
My days no be few? So stop and leave me alone, so dat I go get small comfort,
before I go where I no go return from, to di land of darkness and di shadow of death,
di land wey dark like midnight, of di shadow of death, without any order, where light dey like midnight.’”
